challenges.name: nginx-static-cache-limits-quiz
challenges.title: Read the static, cache and limit config
challenges.description: Three statements about how Rice Rocket's nginx serves the web app, which headers it adds, and what its login rate limit really does. Decide whether each one is true.
hints: For each statement, find the one location that handles the request, then ask which directives that location has of its own and which it inherits.
Look at the levels where `add_header` appears, at the last parameter of `try_files`, and at the numbers in `rate=` and `burst=`.

Same rules on different input: with `location /img/ { add_header X-Robots-Tag noindex; }` under a server that adds `Referrer-Policy`, a 200 from /img/ carries X-Robots-Tag only; and `try_files $uri /404.html` serves /404.html for a missing file without changing the URL in the browser.

questions.explanation: False. add_header directives are inherited from the outer level only if the current level has no add_header of its own. The location defines one, so its responses carry only Cache-Control and lose both security headers. The common reading is that add_header appends to the inherited list; nginx replaces the list per level. Repeat the security headers in the location (or use expires 1y there instead of add_header, so the location has no add_header and inherits the server ones).

questions.question:
The web app is a single-page app. Its build output and the location that serves it:

```text
/usr/share/nginx/html/index.html
/usr/share/nginx/html/assets/index-4f9a2c.js
```

```nginx
location / {
    try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html;
}
```

Statement: "A request for `/orders/42` gets `index.html` with status 200, and the address bar still shows `/orders/42`, so the app's router can render order 42."
questions.explanation: True. Neither the file /orders/42 nor a directory /orders/42/ exists, so try_files makes an internal redirect to its last parameter, /index.html. An internal redirect happens inside nginx: the browser receives the shell with 200 and never sees a new URL, so the client-side router reads /orders/42. The misconception is that this is an HTTP redirect (301/302); it is not, and that is exactly why deep links work.

False. nodelay only means that requests inside the burst are not spaced out: the first request plus the 5 burst slots (6 in total) go to the api at once, and the other 14 are rejected straight away with limit_req_status, 503 by default (set 429). The bucket then refills at the rate, one slot every 6 seconds for 10r/m. A common misconception is that nodelay disables or defers the limit; it changes only the delay of requests that are within the burst.

challenges.name: nginx-static-cache-limits-default-conf
challenges.title: Serve the app, cache it right and limit logins
challenges.description: After each deploy users get a blank page (yesterday's index.html, cached for a day, asks for hashed bundles that no longer exist), deep links like `/orders/42` return 404, and a credential-stuffing burst hit `/api/login` with 2,000 requests a minute. Assemble the fixed default.conf: (1) app routes that are not files (e.g. `/orders/42`) get `/index.html` with 200; a missing file under `/assets/` is a 404, never HTML; (2) `/index.html` (also when reached as `/` or as the fallback) must revalidate on every load (no-cache or max-age=0), files under `/assets/` are cached for at least 30 days (1 year recommended); (3) every static 200 response keeps `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`; (4) gzip covers HTML, CSS, JavaScript, SVG and the api's JSON, but not PNG; (5) `/api/login` allows 10 requests a minute per client IP, with a burst of 5 served without delay, and rejects the excess with 429; other api endpoints are not limited. Run grades it with a simulator that answers each request (status, file served, Cache-Control, gzip, rate limit, nosniff); request times `t` are seconds. The editor starts from the finished file with key blocks missing (`[ ] label` lines): fill each one by clicking a piece, or drag it onto the line on desktop. Some pieces are wrong on purpose.
hints: Which location answers `/index.html` when it is reached through the try_files fallback, and does that location have an `add_header` of its own?

Compare the pieces that fill the same line: the last parameter of each `try_files`, whether a location sets an `add_header` of its own (and so drops the server-level one), and which location carries `limit_req`.

Same tools on a docs site: `location = /docs/index.html { expires -1; }`, `location /docs/_static/ { try_files $uri =404; expires 30d; }`, and for a password-reset form `limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=reset:1m rate=3r/m;` with `limit_req zone=reset burst=2 nodelay; limit_req_status 429;` in `location = /api/password-reset`.

tests.name: Hashed assets are cached for a long time; index.html (also as /) revalidates
Deep links get the app shell; a deleted hashed asset is a 404, not HTML
8 logins from one IP in the same second: 6 reach the api, 2 get 429
Every static 200 keeps X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, cached or not
JS, CSS, SVG, HTML and api JSON are gzipped; PNG is not
The login limit is per IP, leaves other endpoints alone and refills at 10 a minute
